readings_ruling: The dispatch asked five questions. All five check out. (1) IsDeveloping is the paper's own notion, not a reading. Ch. 1 Prop. 2 (ch1 l.357-362) defines the projection of an « ouvert étalé au-dessus de R^n » as « une application p de V dans R^n dont tous les jets appartiennent à J(V) ». p. 238 (ch1 l.402-404) says the structure of an ouvert étalé is « l'unique structure telle que la projection soit un morphisme ». IsDeveloping (GAR n) p is word for word ∀ x, jet x p ∈ jets, and isDeveloping_iff_isGXMorphism (strict, Developing.lean:121) makes it the morphism form. « sur » is not read as « onto ». That is weaker, so the Lean covers both readings. (2) « Generating for the whole group » is weaker than or equal to the paper. The hypothesis is ⋃ g ∈ ⊤, g • E = univ over GXAut (GAR n), which is Déf. 15's « domaine générateur pour G » (ch1 l.419-427). The statement's « balayable » means G itself, and a domain for a subgroup G₁ satisfies ⋃_{g∈G₁} gE = V ⊆ ⋃_{g∈G} gE (strict IsBalayableFor.mono). So no reading is stronger than the Lean's. Compactness is IsCompact with no Hausdorffness, which is again weaker. (3) Déf. 14's segment is the paper's notion. IsAffSegment n Sg M N is IsGXSegment over GAR n: a compatible chart φ with Sg ⊆ φ.source (the open O), M, N ∈ φ.source, and φ '' Sg = segment ℝ (φ M) (φ N). That is ch1 l.410-415 (« un voisinage ouvert O de S, et une carte compatible φ de O, telle que φ(S) = (φ(M), φ(N)) »), and it is the graduated strict definition (Classes.lean:172). The paper's conclusion does not require M ≠ N, and neither does the Lean. (4) The n = 0 counterexample is genuine, not vacuous, and it does not depend on any convention. V = R^0 is one point: connected, Hausdorff and second countable, so it is inside every reading of « variété », Bourbaki's « compact » included. p = id is developing. E = V is compact and generating (the identity suffices). K = R^0 is compact. Every N has p(N) ∈ K. The paper never says n ≥ 1 (Ch. 1 even names S(0) at ch1 l.192), and its proof uses a line of R^n in cases a and b. Unlike T-bz-c2-mesure's n = 0 point, which hinges on Déf. 1 giving coincident points no cross-ratio, this one has no convention to absorb it. Under OQ-45 only option (a) lifts it (finding 2). (5) [Nonempty V] is already ruled. DEC-128 (« variété » is nonempty, extending DEC-114's ruling for an affine space) covers it, so it is not an open reading (finding 1).

labels.label: bzprop:c2s3p1_projection_non_bornee
labels.notes: Correctly left UNMARKED and correctly reported as status partial. No Lean statement can be at least the printed one, because the printed one is false at n = 0. The strongest true form is the combination of three theorems, and that is what the file proves. (i) ProjectionNonBorneePrinted n (l.543) is the printed statement. It quantifies over every V : Type with [TopologicalSpace] [ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ)] [HasGroupoid (affGroupoid n)] [Nonempty], every developing p, every compact generating E (whole group) and every compact K, and concludes ∃ Sg M N, IsAffSegment n Sg M N ∧ M ∈ E ∧ p N ∉ K. Hypothesis by hypothesis it is the printed sentence (l.648-654, checked against the scan, p. 256 = PDF p. 29), with no Hausdorff, connected or countability assumption. The only universe restriction is V : Type, which is disclosed. projectionNonBorneePrinted_iff (l.552) proves it holds iff 0 < n. (ii) projection_non_bornee (l.351) states the same conclusion under exactly the printed hypotheses plus [NeZero n] (disclosed, and forced by the finding) and [Nonempty V] (ruled by DEC-128). Its conclusion is the printed one. (iii) projection_non_bornee_of_ne_univ (l.478) covers every dimension when K ≠ univ. Together they prove the statement in every case except n = 0 with K = R^0, and that case is the counterexample. Non-vacuity: projection_non_bornee_hypotheses_model (R^n, p = id, E = {0}, swept by translations) satisfies the hypotheses for every n. The conclusion is not trivially inhabited: a degenerate segment {M} only helps when p(E) ⊄ K, and the paper's statement is equally weak there. not_isBounded_range_of_isBalayable is the corollary for result B (« une projection non bornée »). It is an extra, not tied to the row. No bold mark appears anywhere in the file. A ``**`…`**`` regex over the whole file and over its first 4000 characters finds nothing. The label line (l.10, character 451) is written unmarked. The bold « **not marked** » and « **Proposition 1.** » do not match the ledger's label regex. If the author rules OQ-45 (a), the REPORT's plan stands: mark Benzecri.projection_non_bornee as it is, since [Nonempty V] is already DEC-128.

docstring_contract: Checked against lean-causal kb/0006. Title at l.4. The label at l.10 is written unmarked as `bzprop:c2s3p1_projection_non_bornee` — `benzecri1960_ch2.tex:648`; l.648 is \begin{prop}[1]. The French quotes (l.20-36) are verbatim against the transcription and the scan, pp. 256-257, with fractions linearised and elisions marked […]. The proof-quote header has a range slip (finding 4). The file has a ## Hypothesis checklist, a ## SCOPE (disclosed) and the Provenance line. One checklist row lacks the contract keyword (finding 3). Every SCOPE claim is true. (a) The n = 0 finding: see readings_ruling (4). (b) The 1° slip at l.682-683: the scan, p. 256, prints fa/fb < k, as transcribed. With f, a, b in order on l, the extensions (M, B) ⊇ (A, B) give m ∈ )f, a]. sup ma/ab = fa/ab is not attained, so 1° holds iff fa/ab ≤ k. From x = fa/fb < k one gets fa/ab = x/(1−x) < k/(1−k) for k < 1, and nothing for k ≥ 1. The finding is true, and the proposed corrections (fa/ab < k, or a close to f) are right. (c) The Hausdorffness remark, argued and not formalized, checked by hand on the line with two origins. It is étalé over R by p and swept from {0₁, 1} by x ↦ ax (a ≠ 0) and the swap of the origins. It has no closed L mapped homeomorphically onto R, since such an L contains one origin and ℝ*, so the other origin lies in its closure. Its p⁻¹(R) = V is connected with p(V) = R, which matches neither )f, g( nor )f, ∞(. So the printed 1° does use Hausdorffness, while the theorem assumes none. This is rightly a remark, not a finding, because « variété » is read Hausdorff.

findings.what: The [Nonempty V] reading is presented as an open question, justified by CAMPAIGN.md's standing reading « variété » = connected. It is already ruled: DEC-128 (« « variété » is nonempty (as DEC-114 for an affine space) »). The justification given is also not sufficient on its own. Connectedness implies nonemptiness in Mathlib's ConnectedSpace, but not in the period's (Bourbaki's) sense, where ∅ is connected.
findings.fix: Cite DEC-128 in the checklist row and in the REPORT, and drop the question. Then OQ-45 (a) is the only obstacle to the mark, as the notes say.
